blurb: Large blue-eyed colourpoint cat famous for going limp when picked up
description: The Ragdoll is a large American cat breed with a semi-long, silky colourpoint coat and blue eyes, known for a docile, placid and affectionate temperament.
answer: The Ragdoll is a large cat breed developed in California in the 1960s by breeder Ann Baker. It has a semi-long, silky colourpoint coat and large blue eyes. Its name comes from its tendency to go limp and relaxed when picked up, and it is best known for a docile, affectionate nature.

body: The breed began in Riverside, California, with Josephine, a non-pedigreed white longhaired cat whose later kittens showed a placid temperament. All Ragdolls descend from Baker's cats. Baker trademarked the name and set up her own registry, the IRCA, around 1971. In 1975 a group led by Denny and Laura Dayton broke away and developed the standard now accepted by registries such as the CFA and FIFe. The breed is particularly popular in the UK and the US.

The Ragdoll is one of the largest domestic breeds: females weigh about 3.6 to 6.8 kg and males 5.4 to 9.1 kg or more, and it can take up to four years to mature. The silky, medium-long coat lacks a dense undercoat. Colours are seal, chocolate, red, blue, lilac and cream, in colourpoint, mitted and bicolour patterns, with lynx and tortie variants. Kittens are born white and colour up over time.

Breed publicity describes the Ragdoll as affectionate, intelligent, relaxed, gentle and an easy-to-handle lap cat. Often called dog-like, many follow their owners from room to room, can learn to retrieve toys and stay playful into old age. The idea that Ragdolls are pain resistant is a myth.
Its long coat usually needs brushing at least twice a week, and shedding may increase in spring. The CFA notes that the lack of a dense undercoat reduces matting.

A 2025 UK study of over 21,000 Ragdolls found a median age at death of 12.85 years, comparable to non-pedigree cats. Conditions reported in the breed include hypertrophic cardiomyopathy linked to the R820W mutation, for which genetic testing is widespread, and urate bladder stones.

They lack a dense undercoat, which the CFA says reduces shedding and matting, but shedding may increase in spring.
